core_obligations: Reduce the exponent n to prime factors (proof lines 15832-15845): from n = ell n' build the short exact sequence 0 -> M[ell] -> M -> M' -> 0 of finite Lambda-modules with M' annihilated by n', and use the associated long exact cohomology sequence to run induction on n.

Reduce the coefficient ring to Lambda/ell Lambda (proof lines 15847-15856): since ell annihilates M, the cohomology of F as a Lambda-module coincides with its cohomology as a Lambda/ellLambda-module, by the identification of cohomology of modules and abelian sheaves in the sites chapter.

Reduce M to a finite free module (proof lines 15858-15875): choose 0 -> N -> Lambda^{oplus m} -> M -> 0, use the exact sequence H^q(underline Lambda^{oplus m}) -> H^q(underline M) -> H^{q+1}(underline N) and descending induction on q, the induction being anchored by the vanishing in degrees > 2 from the vanishing theorem.

Reduce to the constant sheaf underline Lambda, ell annihilating Lambda (proof lines 15877-15906): choose a basis Lambda = direct sum of F_ell e_i with e_0 = 1, use underline Lambda = direct sum of underline F_ell e_i and the commutation of cohomology with direct sums (the colimit theorem, or its lemma form, or the bounded-below direct sum lemma), and conclude finiteness of H^q(X, underline F_ell) by the finiteness part of the vanishing theorem, with the prime-to-characteristic and the properness hypotheses covering the two assertions of the statement.
proof_roadmap: Induct on n by splitting off one prime factor and using the long exact sequence.
Replace Lambda by Lambda/ell Lambda and then M by a finite free module, using descending induction on q and the vanishing above the dimension of the curve.

Finally compute with the constant sheaf underline Lambda written as a direct sum of copies of underline F_ell, commuting cohomology with the direct sum, and invoke the finiteness of H^q(X, underline F_ell) in the two cases of the statement.
difficulty_reason: The lemma establishes finiteness of H^q_etale(X, underline M) for a constant coefficient sheaf on a separated finite type curve over an algebraically closed field, in the two cases named in the statement (statement lines 15817-15829). Its content is a chain of explicit reductions (proof lines 15831-15906): first from n to the prime factors of n by a long exact sequence, then from Lambda to Lambda/ell Lambda, then from M to a finite free module by descending induction on q anchored by the vanishing above the dimension of the curve, and finally a basis trick writing underline Lambda as a direct sum of copies of underline F_ell and using that cohomology commutes with direct sums. H2: several standard reductions, each written out, none of them a long construction.
